Quick technical background — telemetry we collect: anonymized token counts, request latencies, error rates, and aggregated model usage.

- Billing events: aggregated token counts tied to customer tenancy; we can provide monthly usage reports and do not provide telemetry to third parties for marketing.
- Product improvement: we do optional logging for model quality improvements; for enterprise customers we can disable that by default or process it under a separate opt-in with retention controls.
- Subprocessors: infra providers (cloud GPUs, metrics/store) may be listed; some are US-only, a few have multi-region presence (US/EU).

Risks: if we say 'telemetry never a sale', that seems reasonable if telemetry is not used for targeted advertising or monetization beyond billing and product ops. Need legal to define sale carve-out precisely (what 'sell' means vs 'use').

I can extract the latest subprocessor CSV and flag entries that handle logging/metrics by EOD today.

Subject: Draft CPRA addendum language (telemetry / subprocessor notice)

Evelyn / Dev — below is proposed language to start with; I focused on aligning with 'service provider / processor' terminology and adding a telemetry carve-out and a subprocessor notice period:

--- Proposed CPRA Addendum clauses ---
1. Definition of "Sale": For the avoidance of doubt, the parties agree that the term "sell", "sale", or "selling" as used in the California Consumer Privacy Act and the California Privacy Rights Act does not include: (a) the disclosure or transfer of Customer's Service Usage Data, aggregated or pseudonymized telemetry, performance metrics, or billing records by Redwood Inference to the extent such data is used solely to provide, maintain, secure, or bill for the Services and not to target advertising; or (b) disclosures to Processor-identified Subprocessors for the sole purpose of providing the Services on Customer's behalf.

2. Telemetry and Product Improvement: Redwood will process telemetry and logs for product improvement only with Customer's prior written consent. For enterprise healthcare customers, Redwood will default product-improvement logging to disabled; if enabled, data will be pseudonymized and retained only as specified in the Service Agreement.

3. Subprocessor Notice and Objection: Redwood will provide Customer at least thirty (30) calendar days' prior notice of the addition of any new Subprocessor that will process Personal Data in the United States. Customer may object in writing within fifteen (15) calendar days on reasonable grounds related to compliance with applicable law or data protection obligations; the parties will meet in good faith to resolve the objection.

4. Transfers and Location Restrictions: Redwood will not transfer Customer Personal Data to countries or service providers that would cause Customer to violate material obligations under applicable US state law or Acme Health's internal policies without Customer's prior written approval.

--- end ---

Notes: I left an explicit 'targeted advertising' carve-out because that's the CPRA focus. We may need to decide whether product-improvement telemetry is "processing" or a sale when aggregated. Also, keep an audit trail for subprocessor notices — we should log notices and any objections.

If this looks OK, I can convert into track-changes and prepare the redline for Acme.

— Lauren Bishop
Senior Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
